Good morning, and welcome to our session today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm here to support you during this significant period in your life. As we navigate the ups and downs of new motherhood together, I want to assure you that everything discussed in this room will remain confidential and respected.

To better understand your emotional well-being and ensure you're receiving the best possible care, we'll be using the EPDS today. The EPDS is a valuable tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's essential to acknowledge that becoming a new mother can bring about a wide range of emotions, and it's perfectly okay to feel overwhelmed or unsure at times.

Please know that you're in a safe and supportive space, where you can openly share your feelings without judgment. Our goal is to provide you with the care and resources you need to thrive during this time. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us gain a better understanding of your emotional state over the past seven days.

We'll take this one question at a time, and I encourage you to answer as honestly as you can. Remember, this is about supporting you and ensuring your well-being. So, let's begin. The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to?

.. to be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, and my baby does make me smile, but it's just not the same as before. I feel like I've lost a little bit of myself, you know? I used to be the one who could always find the humor in things, but now it's like I have to try really hard to feel that way. And even when I do laugh, it's not as carefree as it used to be. There's always this underlying worry, like I'm waiting for something to go wrong. It's hard to explain, but I just don't feel as lighthearted as I used to. And it's been really frustrating for me, because I want to be happy and enjoy this time with my baby, but it's just not coming as easily as I thought it would. (sighs) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I haven't been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as I used to. Like I said, it's just not the same. I feel like I'm going through the motions a lot of the time, and even when I do try to laugh or find the humor in something, it feels forced. I'm just so tired and worried all the time, it's hard to really enjoy things like I used to. And when I do have a moment where I feel happy or carefree, it's quickly replaced by anxiety or guilt. It's like I'm constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? (pauses, looking down) It's hard to explain, but I just feel really overwhelmed and unsure of myself most of the time.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong. As a new mom, I feel like I'm supposed to have everything together, and when things don't go according to plan, I immediately think it's my fault. I'll be like, "If only I had done this differently, or if only I had been more prepared..." It's like I'm constantly criticizing myself, and it's really hard to shake off that feeling of guilt. Even when my baby cries or isn't sleeping well, I'll think to myself, "I must be doing something wrong, I'm not a good enough mother..." It's a really hard feeling to deal with, and it makes me feel even more anxious and unsure of myself. (looks down, fidgeting with hands) Sometimes I feel like I'm just not cut out for this, and that's a really scary thought.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I've been anxious or worried for no good reason a lot lately. It's like my mind is always racing, thinking about all the things that could go wrong with the baby, or with my health, or with our future... It's exhausting, to be honest. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something ridiculous, like "What if the baby stops breathing?" or "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" And then I'll start to feel anxious and my heart will start racing, and it's hard to calm myself down. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll feel like I'm going to panic. It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is constantly looking for things to worry about, even when everything is fine. (takes a deep breath) It's really overwhelming, and it's hard to enjoy the moments with my baby when I'm always worried about something.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason. It's like, out of nowhere, I'll just feel this wave of fear or panic wash over me. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel like I'm not in control. Other times, it's when I'm trying to fall asleep, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios. It's hard to breathe, and my heart will be racing, and I'll just feel like I'm going to lose it. (starts to tear up) It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear, like something is going to happen to them, or to me, or to us. (pauses, taking a deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. (wipes away tears) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about...
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... things have been getting on top of me. It feels like everything is just piling up, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, recovering from childbirth, trying to manage the household... it's all just so overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be trying to do one thing, like feeding the baby, and then I'll think about all the other things I need to do, like laundry and cleaning and cooking, and it just feels like too much. (sighs) I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, and I'm always behind. And on top of that, I'm just so tired all the time. I'm not sleeping well, and when I do sleep, I'm always worried that the baby will wake up and need me. It's like I'm just running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank. (looks down, shaking head) Sometimes I feel like I'm just not doing anything well, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping. It's like my mind is always racing, and I just can't seem to turn it off. I'll be lying in bed, trying to fall asleep, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that are worrying me, or all the things that I'm not doing well as a mom. And then I'll start to feel anxious, and my heart will start racing, and it's just impossible to relax. Sometimes I'll be awake for hours, just lying there, feeling miserable and overwhelmed. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious or scared, and I'll just lie there, staring at the ceiling, feeling like I'm all alone. (pauses, looking down) It's hard to explain, but it's like my unhappiness is just weighing me down, and it's making it hard for me to do even the simplest things, like sleep. (sighs) I just feel so tired, all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm finally turning a corner," but then the next day will come, and I'll be back to feeling miserable again. (shakes head) It's just really hard.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I have felt sad or miserable. It's like a cloud is just following me around all the time. I'll be doing okay, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. Sometimes it's triggered by something, like a difficult feeding session or a blowout diaper, but other times it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, I just feel so overwhelmed and sad. (starts to tear up) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling the weight of everything, and it's crushing me. Being a new mom is so much harder than I thought it would be, and I just feel like I'm not doing it right. I feel like I'm failing the baby, and I'm failing myself. (pauses, wiping away tears) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby, but instead I just feel sad and anxious and overwhelmed. It's like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it. (sighs) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about...
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I have been so unhappy that I have been crying. It's like the tears just come out of nowhere, and I don't even know why I'm crying half the time. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like my emotions are just so close to the surface, and it doesn't take much to set me off. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes it's because I'm feeling guilty or anxious. And sometimes it's just because I'm feeling so sad and alone. (starts to cry) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and the tears are just a release of all the emotions that are building up inside me. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling so much all the time, and I don't know how to process it all. (pauses, wiping away tears) I've been crying a lot lately, just little bursts of tears throughout the day. It's embarrassing, because sometimes my husband will be like, "What's wrong?" and I'll be like, "I don't know, I just am." (sighs) It's just really hard to deal with, you know? I feel like I'm supposed to be strong and capable, but instead I just feel weak and emotional all the time.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down) Yes... the thought of harming myself has occurred to me. It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've ever thought about before, but lately, it's just been there, lurking in the back of my mind. It's like, when things get really overwhelming, and I feel like I just can't do this anymore, the thought will pop into my head. It's not like I've ever seriously considered it, or made a plan or anything, but it's just... it's just a thought that's there. (looks up, tears in her eyes) And it's scary, because I don't know why I'm thinking it, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's like, I know I'm a good person, and I would never actually hurt myself, but the fact that the thought is even there is just... it's just really frightening. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I guess I just feel like I'm losing myself, you know? Like, I'm just disappearing into this new role as a mom, and I don't know who I am anymore. And that thought, it's just... it's just a manifestation of all the fear and anxiety and uncertainty that I'm feeling. (looks down, her voice barely above a whisper) I'm just so scared, and I don't know what to do.

The patient is experiencing a range of symptoms that are concerning for postpartum depression, including feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, anxiety, and guilt. She reports difficulty coping with daily responsibilities, sleep disturbances, and frequent crying spells. The patient also expressed thoughts of self-harm, which is a significant safety concern. It's essential to approach this situation with empathy and understanding, acknowledging the challenges of the postpartum period and the need for support.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 28, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Definitely not so much now' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a lack of communication, which cannot be scored directly, but given the context and the nature of the question, it suggests the patient is not able to look forward with enjoyment to things, aligning with 'Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>The patient explicitly states they blame themselves unnecessarily when things go wrong, and describes a pattern of constant self-criticism and guilt, indicating this happens 'most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent and intense feelings of fear and panic, often without a clear reason, and experiences physical symptoms such as a racing heart and difficulty breathing, indicating a high level of distress.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all'. The patient explicitly states that 'it feels like everything is just piling up, and I don't know how to keep up' and 'I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, and I'm always behind', demonstrating a significant difficulty in managing their responsibilities.</sym>, <sym>Patient explicitly states they have been unhappy and had difficulty sleeping, with their mind racing and feeling anxious, indicating a high level of distress matching 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the guideline option 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having the thought of harming herself, describing it as occurring when things get overwhelming, but clarifies it's not something she's seriously considered or planned, matching the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and emotional concerns are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 28 indicates a high risk of depression, and the presence of suicidal thoughts necessitates urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. The patient's feelings of overwhelm, anxiety, and guilt are common symptoms of postpartum depression, and her sleep disturbances and crying spells further support this screening impression. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to share feelings and concerns with her support system
3. Develop a safety plan to address self-harm thoughts
4. Recommend sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep quality
5. Provide resources for postpartum depression support groups and online communities
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

Recommendations for further assessment and support will be provided to the patient, with a focus on addressing her emotional and psychological needs during the postpartum period.
